title: Untitled (Your assignment is to divide and conquer) [Postcard]

description.main: A Fotofolio postcard reproducing Barbara Kruger's Untitled (Your assignment is to divide and conquer) (1981), a found black-and-white photograph of a face seen through a blind, with the text in white Futura Bold Oblique on red. Published in New York by Fotofolio; 15 x 11 cm.
description.extended:
A Fotofolio postcard reproducing Barbara Kruger's Untitled (Your assignment is to divide and conquer) (1981), one of the earliest of the red-bordered photograph-and-text works that have defined her practice since the early 1980s.

The image is a found black-and-white photograph of a man's face seen through the slats of a drawn blind. White Futura Bold Oblique runs across the top on a red band and the last word, "conquer," sits alone in a box at the foot of the picture. The source work, a photograph in the artist's frame at 147.3 by 103.8 cm, was shown at the Whitney's Downtown Branch in 1982 and illustrated in the catalogue of her 1983 ICA London show We Won't Play Nature to Your Culture.

Kruger (b. 1945) was a designer and picture editor at Condé Nast magazines before turning, around 1979, to found photographs overlaid with her own text. Fotofolio, founded in New York in 1975 by Julie Galant and Martin Bondell, issued several of her images as postcards alongside its history-of-photography series.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) worked as a graphic designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines including Mademoiselle before turning around 1979 to found photographs overlaid with her own text, set in Futura Bold Oblique or Helvetica Ultra Condensed. She is associated with the Pictures Generation; her first institutional show was at the ICA London in 1983 and the retrospective Thinking of You. I Mean Me. I Mean You. toured the Art Institute of Chicago, LACMA and MoMA 2021-22.

notes: Acquired from Printed Matter, New York: https://www.printedmatter.org/catalog/50247. Not signed. Printed Matter stock 111777 C; the record gives no publication year for the card (Fotofolio, New York; [1] p.; 15 x 11 cm; colour). Source work: Untitled (Your assignment is to divide and conquer), 1981, black and white photograph in artist's frame, 147.3 x 103.8 cm; exhibited Whitney Museum of American Art Downtown Branch, Frames of Reference, May-June 1982, cat. no. 5; illustrated in the ICA London catalogue We Won't Play Nature to Your Culture (1983), p. 47, which the library holds (id 605); provenance Larry Gagosian Gallery, Los Angeles, and Max Protetch, New York; sold Sotheby's New York 15 November 2019, lot 494, so in private hands. Kruger has no official website; artist link is her gallery, Spruth Magers.
